title: How I know when my app breaks: not more testing, Sentry.
hook: Your app breaks. Who tells you?
summary: Sentry error tracking: how I know when my app breaks, not more testing.
body: Sentry error tracking: how I know when my app breaks, not more testing.

Tests check your code once, before it ships. Nothing checks it once it's live. Sentry does: when I stopped a project on Vercel it flagged "this website is no longer reachable", and it caught the globe in Atlaria not loading for people.
I'm Manraj Sidhu, AI developer, and this is the real build.

Setup is five steps: run the wizard, add an uptime monitor, send alerts to Slack or email, upload source maps, throw a test error. Save this before you ship again.
Which dev myth would you call out? "Just test it more" is mine.

Comment SENTRY and I'll send you the link.
Follow @manrajtalks for more of The Stack.
guide: Set up error and uptime monitoring so you hear about a broken app from a tool, not from a user. You need a live web app (for example on Vercel), a free Sentry account and a Slack workspace or an email address.
1. Create a project in Sentry for your framework and run the Sentry install wizard in your app's folder.
1. Add an uptime monitor in Sentry that checks your live URL, so you are told if the site stops being reachable.
1. Send alerts to Slack or email so a failure reaches you without you opening a dashboard.
1. Upload source maps so errors point to your real code rather than minified output.
1. Throw a deliberate test error in the app and confirm it appears in Sentry and triggers an alert.
1. Stop a test deployment on Vercel and confirm the "no longer reachable" alert arrives.
Watch out: tests only check your code once, before it ships, so don't treat a passing test run as a sign the live app is healthy.
